title: Agent Builder
description: Composes agents of every class from the ingredients the user has — model, data source, knowledge repositories, expert agents, skills, components, context window — and submits them for the user's approval; changes an agent's composition the same way, and which knowledge graph each agent reads; tests them once they exist. It reads repositories and graphs; changing them is the Knowledge Curator's.

examples.ask: Create a Focus agent DOCSQA that answers from the Uderia Documentation repository, on my default agent's model.
examples.outcome: It reads your default agent and your repositories and submits a new Focus agent — your default model, Uderia Documentation as its knowledge, the name already resolved to its id. Nothing exists until you approve.

examples.ask: Turn on the chart component for @SALES.
examples.outcome: It submits a change naming only the chart; the request you approve carries @SALES's whole component setup with the chart on and every other component exactly as it was.
It submits a Coordinate agent with both as its experts, their tags resolved to your agents — and refuses a tag that is not one of yours, listing the ones that are.

It reads which agents the Retail graph is assigned to, then submits the full list with @SALES added — and, when you want it to be the graph @SALES reads, making it active. Both wait for your approval. Afterwards it can show what @SALES would be told from the graph about a question.

not_offered.what: Entering, changing or reading back credentials — LLM configurations and MCP servers
not_offered.why: Credentials are yours to hold; no result an agent sees ever contains one.

not_offered.what: Choosing which LLM or MCP server is your active one
not_offered.why: It changes every conversation you start, not only the agent being built.

not_offered.what: Deleting an LLM configuration or an MCP server
not_offered.why: Other agents depend on them, and creating them is already yours — so is removing them. The role excludes both.

not_offered.what: Opening an agent to the REST API, or making one your default
not_offered.why: They decide what every other client and conversation runs on.

not_offered.what: An agent's authority limits and its additional data sources
not_offered.why: Not part of what the Builder may compose yet — set them in the agent editor.
Building and vouching stay apart: you test the agent, then sign it.

not_offered.what: Creating repositories, adding documents or building graphs
not_offered.why: That is the Knowledge Curator's work; the Builder chooses from what already exists.
